# Homework 02 — Project Design and Graphing

### How to turn it in

You have **not** learned Quarto yet, so for this one: run your code in an R
script, and paste your **code and your figures** into a Word document to submit.
(From Homework 05 on, you'll submit a rendered Quarto report instead.)

::: callout-tip
## Loading the data — two options

**Local** — put the file in your project's `data/` folder:

``` r
library(readxl)
library(tidyverse)
tree_df <- read_excel("data/2026_06_25_tree_experiment_raw_data.xlsx")
```

**From GitHub (no download)** — a CSV copy lives in the course data repo; read it straight from the raw link:

``` r
tree_df <- read_csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wlperry/umd_datasci/main/data/tree_experiment.csv")
```

*(Only CSVs can be read from a URL — Excel files must be local. Adjust the repo/branch in the link to match yours.)*
:::

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Task 1 — Inspect (1 pt)

Load the data and run `glimpse(tree_df)`. Write one sentence: what does one row represent, and how many rows are there?

### Task 2 — A basic boxplot (2 pts)

Make a boxplot of `weight_g` (y) by `side` (x). Add clear axis labels and a title.

### Task 3 — The twist: show the raw points (2 pts)

We only made a plain boxplot in class. **Figure out** how to overlay the individual leaves on top of the boxes using `geom_point()` with `position = position_jitter(width = 0.15)`, and make the points semi-transparent with `alpha`. *(Hint: the points layer comes after the boxplot layer.)*

### Task 4 — The twist continues: facet (2 pts)

Using `mutate()`, add a column `size_class` that is `"large"` when `weight_g > 5` and `"small"` otherwise. Then remake your boxplot with `facet_wrap(~ size_class)`. What do you notice?

### Task 5 — Save it (1 pt)

Save your final figure to a `figures/` folder as a PNG at `dpi = 300` using `ggsave()`.

### Task 6 — Interpret (2 pts)

In 2–3 sentences: based on your plots, does one side of the tree appear to have heavier leaves? What would you want to test formally next?

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Grading notes *(instructor — remove before posting)*

10 pts: T1 (1) · T2 correct boxplot + labels (2) · T3 jittered points added (2) · T4 mutate + facet (2) · T5 ggsave dpi=300 (1) · T6 sensible interpretation (2). The "struggle" is discovering `position_jitter` and `facet_wrap` on their own.

*End of Homework 02.*
